review_candidates.title: Network Engineer
review_candidates.description: About Citadel Aviation Citadel Aviation has grown from a startup vision into a global leader in V/VVIP aircraft completions, maintenance, modifications, and luxury interiors. Located in Lake Charles, Dallas, and serving customers onsite where they're at, our teams deliver work on some of the most sophisticated narrow and wide body aircraft in the world. We have significantly expanded project volume since 2019, and that growth was built by people who take pride in doing the work right. Whatever your role, Citadel is a place to bring what you know and build what comes next. Purpose Information technology is foundational to how Citadel Aviation operates at every site, from the systems that move work across the hangar floor and the shops to the platforms that support administrative staff. Reliable, secure network and voice infrastructure enables Citadel to operate without interruption, protect its work and its people, and meet its obligations to customers and partners. This role owns the design, operation, and lifecycle of Citadel's network and voice infrastructure across every Citadel site, spanning multiple states, including the turn-up of new facilities as the company grows. The Network Engineer is the company's single internal owner of firewalls, switching, wireless, VPN and remote access, internet and backup connectivity, voice, and the network integrations that connect facility and operational systems. The role reports to the IT Manager, Infrastructure and Support, partners closely with the Cybersecurity Engineer on network security standards, owns assigned IT projects, and is accountable for the reliability and performance of the network at every site. Citadel's multi-site network is built on next-generation firewalls, enterprise switching and wireless, and a VOIP calling platform, with redundant internet connectivity at each site and connectivity to an off-site disaster-recovery environment. Identity and collaboration run on Microsoft 365, servers run on a virtualized platform, and security operations are delivered in partnership with an external managed detection and response (MDR) provider. Essential Job Functions Own the design, operation, and lifecycle of Citadel's network infrastructure across all sites: firewalls, core and access switching, wireless, internet connectivity, and backup connectivity. Maintain current firmware, configuration standards, and documentation. Lead network design and turn-up for new Citadel facilities. Standardize the network design across all sites so each site is built, monitored, and supported the same way, and maintain the network section of Citadel's new-site playbook so the standard build is repeatable. Perform hands-on cabling and hardware installation as needed during site turn-up and network upgrades. Provide network assessment, cost estimates, and day-one readiness criteria as input to new facility evaluations and acquisition due diligence. Own secure connectivity between sites, between sites and the cloud, for remote users, and to the disaster-recovery environment, including site-to-site and remote-access VPN. Own the design, operation, and security of Citadel's voice and unified communications infrastructure, including the VOIP calling platform, desk phones, and integration with the company's collaboration and messaging platforms. Own network integrations for facility and operational systems, including access-control, conference room A/V, printers, shop-floor and hangar equipment, and other connected operational devices. Implement secure segmentation for this equipment to the standards set with the Cybersecurity Engineer, and partner with Facilities and Operations on new installations. Operate the firewall and network security controls day to day: rule changes, segmentation, wireless security, and remote-access policy. Implement the network security standards set with the Cybersecurity Engineer and participate in firewall rule review. Monitor network health and capacity. Maintain monitoring and alerting coverage across all sites, review utilization, plan upgrades ahead of demand, and schedule and execute preventive maintenance windows. Own the network components of business continuity and disaster recovery planning, including documented recovery objectives for connectivity, and participate in DR testing. Perform in line with established KPIs and service-level targets, including network availability, incident response and resolution times, change success rate, and project delivery. Track and report performance regularly to IT leadership. Serve as the primary on-call responder for network and voice incidents. Drive diagnosis, coordinate internal and external resources, and engage directly in resolution. Own incident communication for network and voice events. Notify IT leadership and impacted business stakeholders, provide regular status updates throughout an incident, and deliver post-incident summaries with root cause and follow-up actions. Deliver assigned IT projects within networking and voice, and contribute network expertise to broader IT initiatives, including new-site spin-up, acquisitions, office moves, and infrastructure upgrades. Partner with the Cybersecurity Engineer on vulnerability remediation for network devices, security incident investigation, and network evidence for audits and assessments. Partner with the Systems Administrator and the Support team on day-to-day troubleshooting, escalations, and the handoff between endpoint, server, and network issues. Own vendor relationships within the network and voice portfolio, including internet providers, network hardware and support contracts, voice carriers, cabling contractors, and specialized network contractors. Support contract negotiations and renewals, and bring work currently performed by contractors in-house where practical. Own the network and voice operating budget. Track expenses, project upcoming needs (hardware refresh, circuits, licensing, support renewals), and provide input on annual IT budget planning. Maintain network documentation, diagrams, IP address management, configuration backups, runbooks, and asset inventory for all network and voice equipment, along with hardware standards and a lifecycle and refresh schedule. Identify and propose improvements in network design, resilience, monitoring coverage, and cost. Deliver approved initiatives. Requirements Required Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline, or equivalent professional experience. 5+ years of hands-on enterprise network engineering, including experience as the primary owner of a multi-site network. Hands-on experience with next-generation firewalls, enterprise switching, and enterprise wireless. Experience with Palo Alto, Cisco, and Meraki platforms preferred; comparable platforms welcome. Experience with routing, VLAN design, network segmentation, and site-to-site and remote-access VPN. Experience delivering network projects end to end, including at least one site build-out or turn-up, with vendor coordination. Able to work independently, communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders, and travel regionally between Citadel sites. Ability to read and interpret work instructions, standard operating procedures, and safety documentation written in English, and to communicate clearly in English with coworkers and supervisors as required to perform the essential functions of the position. Preferred Cisco (CCNA or CCNP), Palo Alto (PCNSA or PCNSE), or comparable certifications. VOIP or unified communications experience. SD-WAN, zero-trust network access, or network access control (NAC) experience. Datacenter, virtualization, or disaster-recovery connectivity experience. Experience in aviation, aerospace, manufacturing, MRO, or other regulated operational environments. Knowledge, Skills, And Other Attributes Deep technical expertise across enterprise networking: firewalls, routing, switching, wireless, VPN, and voice. Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis discipline across complex, multi-site network incidents. Working knowledge of network security practices sufficient to implement agreed standards and recognize risk in proposed changes. Project delivery and prioritization skills across simultaneous initiatives, with the ability to plan, document, and coordinate technical projects end to end. Strong written and verbal communication, particularly during operational events, and the ability to translate technical concepts for business audiences. Strong organizational, documentation, and operational discipline; works autonomously and makes sound technical decisions in fast-moving situations. Customer service mindset with focus on responsiveness, professionalism, and follow-through; committed to staying current as technologies evolve. Working Conditions This position is considered OFFICE WORK. Almost exclusively indoors during the day and occasionally at night. Occasional exposure to airborne dust in the workplace. Work surface is stable (flat). After-hours and on-call work is required for critical network and voice support, maintenance windows, and incident response. This position is considered LIGHT work, with frequent lifting up to 10 lbs and occasional lifting up to 20 lbs; occasional climbing, stooping, kneeling, squatting, and reaching; frequent standing; and constant repetitive movements of arms and hands and seated work with back supported.
